newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT, Asian firms to take stake in Asia Internet.
newsitem.headline: NTT, Asian firms to take stake in Asia Internet.

text.p: NTT, Telekom Malaysia Bhd and other Asian telecom operators will take stakes in Japanese Internet access provider Asia Internet Holding (AIH) as it upgrades its Asian networks later this year, a spokeswoman for AIH said on Tuesday.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp is expected to take about a 15 percent stake in the Internet access provider for about 240 million yen, she said.
AIH, an affiliate of Japan's largest Internet access provider, Internet Initiative Japan Inc, plans to boost its capital from the current 900 million yen later this year.
AIH is also in talks regarding investment in the firm with Telekom Malaysia, the Communications Authority of Thailand and Chunghwa Telecom Co of Taiwan, she said.
Announcements will be made on August 21, she said.
"We expect the investments to help build closer relationships with Asia's telecom operators," she said.
AIH provides Internet access services by operating backbone networks that connect eight Asian countries, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Hong Kong.
It is discussing a plan to offer an Internet phone service, she said.

After the capital increase, AIH plans to lay networks in Vietnam, China, the Philippines and Australia and upgrade the networks' capacity to 45 megabits per second (Mbps) from the current 1.5 Mbps, she said.
Internet Initiative will remain the biggest shareholder in AIH after the capital increase, she said.
